Base directory for this skill: D:\Apps\micro1-frontier-hackathon\runtime\.claude\skills\aliasbreaker

Run one AliasBreaker campaign following the protocol in CLAUDE.md exactly.

- CASE = the fixture path given in the arguments (e.g.
  `../data/cases/dev/case-101.json`).
- RUN = `runs/<run-id>` if a run id was given, else `runs/<case-id>-manual`.

Begin with `start`, follow the decision guidance, and end with `finalize`.
All hard rules in CLAUDE.md apply unchanged.


ARGUMENTS: ../data/cases/final/case-30001.json runs/final-case-30001-r2
Candidate 4 (P=1.593d) leads with support 0.505, followed by candidate 0 (P=1.059d, 0.206). Let me check diagnostics to see where they separate.

Pair (0,4) has the highest support_product (0.104) — the most important discrimination to make. Slot 2 (t=33.14) hits this pair's best separation (4.0σ) and also discriminates pairs (1,4), (2,4), (2,3). It's the earliest slot covering the top pair, so I'll take it.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --slot 2 --why "Slot 2 gives max separation for the leading pair 0 versus 4, the highest support-product pair, and also discriminates pairs 1-4, 2-4, and 2-3 at the same time, and is the earliest slot offering this coverage"

content.text: Big shift: candidates 3 and 4 collapsed to 0 support. Now candidate 2 leads (0.419), then 1 (0.321), then 0 (0.259). Let me re-run diagnostics.
Slot 6 (t=38.35) is the earliest slot that tops both leading pairs (0,2) and (1,2). Taking it.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --slot 6 --why "Slot 6 is the earliest reachable point offering max separation for both leading pairs 1 versus 2 and 0 versus 2, the two highest support-product pairs after candidates 3 and 4 collapsed"

content.text: Now 0 and 1 are nearly tied (0.506 vs 0.489), candidate 2 collapsed. Need to resolve pair (0,1).
Pair (0,1) is by far the dominant remaining pair. Slot 22 (t=58.12) is the earliest slot offering top separation for it.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --slot 22 --why "Slot 22 is the earliest slot offering maximum separation for the sole remaining live pair 0 versus 1, since candidate 2 has effectively collapsed"

content.text: Candidate 1 now leads (0.704) over candidate 0 (0.284), but not yet at theta=0.997. Need more discrimination.
Pair (0,1) is still the dominant one. Slot 29 (t=71.28) is earliest with top separation.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --slot 29 --why "Confirmation observation at the earliest slot with maximum separation for the still-dominant pair 0 versus 1, since support has not yet crossed the resolution threshold"

content.text: Close, but 0.979 < theta (0.997). Candidate 0 is now negligible; need to squeeze out candidate 2.
Pair (1,2) is now the dominant one (support_product 0.0175 vs 0.0033). Slot 36 (t=80.53) is earliest with top separation.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --slot 36 --why "Targeting the last live pair 1 versus 2 at its earliest maximally separating slot to push candidate 1 support above the resolution threshold"

content.text: Still below theta (0.997) at 0.989. One observation left — let's find the best final shot.
Slot 38 (t=82.17) tops both remaining pairs — the best final shot with our last observation.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --slot 38 --why "Final budgeted observation at the earliest slot with maximum separation for both remaining live pairs to push the leading candidate over the resolution threshold if the true orbit supports it"

content.text: Candidate 1 support is now 0.999995, well above theta (0.997). Resolved. Finalizing.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli finalize --run runs/final-case-30001-r2 --why "Candidate 1 at period 19.349 days reached support 0.999995, far above theta 0.997, after sequentially eliminating candidates 3 and 4 at slot 2, candidate 2 competition at slots 6 and 36, and candidate 0 at slots 22, 29, and 38, all chosen as earliest maximally separating points for the live pairs at each stage"

content.text:
Campaign complete and resolved.

**Result:** Candidate 1 (P = 19.349 days, K ≈ 13.4 m/s) selected with support 0.999995, well above θ = 0.997. All 6 observations used.

**Campaign summary:**
- Started with candidate 4 (P=1.593d) leading on sparse data, but pair (0,4) was the highest-uncertainty pair — the first follow-up at slot 2 (t=33.14) collapsed candidates 3 and 4 to zero support and flipped the leader to candidate 2.
- Slot 6 (t=38.35) then simultaneously discriminated the two strongest remaining pairs (0,2) and (1,2), collapsing candidate 2 and putting candidates 0 and 1 in a near-tie (~0.51 vs ~0.49).
- Three more observations (slots 22, 29, 36), each chosen as the earliest slot offering peak separation for the dominant live pair, progressively pushed candidate 1's support from 0.70 → 0.98 → 0.99.
- A final confirmation at slot 38 pushed support to 0.999995, crossing the strict resolution threshold.

The true orbit alias was far from obvious at the start (candidate 1 wasn't even the initial leader), which is exactly the kind of case this thrifty, pair-targeted strategy is meant to untangle.
